subject: Implementation workback, fallback tiers, and regional placement — EquinoxAI Dedicated pool
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir@equinox.ai>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 1 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Kickoff: Equinox Dedicated pool — workback & regional constraints

Hi Lauren / team,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to kick off the implementation workback for our dedicated GPU pool (EquinoxAI / DL-4521). High-level asks:

- Baseline sustained throughput: 40 tokens/sec across our inference fleet (mixed generation and rerank).
- P95 latency target: <= 200ms for single-turn generation (prompt+stream).
- Primary region preference: us-west-2; secondary in eu-west-1 only if latency can be kept under 300ms.
- Peak burst requirement: ability to scale +2x sustained for up to 30 minutes during product launches.

Could you propose timelines, preferred instance SKUs, and a fallback ordering if capacity is constrained? Also include any SLO caveats around KV cache warmup and cold-starts. Attaching a short traffic forecast.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a call if that helps.

Samir
Samir Shah
Head of Platform
EquinoxAI
[attachment: equinox_traffic_forecast.csv (csv)]

From: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
To: Samir Shah <samir@equinox.ai>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 1 Oct 2028 13:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Equinox Dedicated pool — workback & regional constraints

Samir — thanks for the detail.

We’ll put together a two-week workback + a fallback tiers doc. Quick notes up front:

- Proposed kickoff call: Tue Oct 3, 10:00 PT. Will cover milestones, handoff checkpoints, and security evidence.
- First pass: we’ll size a single primary pool in us-west-2 (A100/RTX-class depending on model quantization) with eu-west-1 cold-fallback.
- Autoscale approach: aggressive vertical burst (GPU warm pools) + horizontal replica scale over a 10–15 minute window.
- KV cache: expect a warm-up window of 2–6 minutes for sustained request patterns; we’ll recommend prefix caching for critical routes.

I’ve attached a draft workback spreadsheet with milestones and owner assignments. Please confirm the kickoff time or propose alternatives.

Thanks,

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Sr. Manager, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
[attachment: equinox_workback_v1.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: aditya.rao@redwood.com
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, Samir Shah <samir@equinox.ai>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 2 Oct 2028 08:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Equinox Dedicated pool — workback & regional constraints

Looping in a few technical considerations ahead of the call:

- Instance SKUs: recommend GA100-80GB for Quant-8 models; fallback to A100-40GB if quota constrained. If Equinox is using fp16/quantized weights we can push to lower-memory GPUs.
- Autoscale policy: target pool baseline (min replicas) sized for 1.2x steady state; burst pool of pre-warmed GPUs for 2x capacity with a 3–5 minute warm window. We should avoid cold-start autoscale for immediate latency-sensitive routes.
- Caching: enable prefix/KV caching for 90% of repeated prompts; design endpoint-level cache TTLs.
- Canary ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 60% over 48–72 hours for initial traffic cutover.

I’ll bring a region-capacity sketch to the kickoff and a shortlist of compatible kernels per model family.

- Aditya
Aditya Rao
Lead, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

From: Samir Shah <samir@equinox.ai>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, aditya.rao@redwood.com
Cc: Kara Lin <kara@equinox.ai>, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Oct 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Equinox Dedicated pool — workback & regional constraints

Thanks Aditya — this is very helpful. A few clarifications following the kickoff:

- Traffic split: 85% US (users routed to us-west-2), 15% EU. EU users are latency sensitive but can tolerate up to 300ms p95.
- Model mix: 60% generation (long-form), 40% short-query/rerank. Generation sessions have higher memory & KV needs.
- SLA ask: would like a soft guarantee on burst capacity during launches (we can accept a short ramp to full burst in 10 minutes if necessary).

We uploaded a CSV with hourly forecast slices for the next 90 days. Please incorporate it into the workback.

Samir

Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 5 Oct 2028 09:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Equinox Dedicated pool — workback & regional constraints

Adding infra constraints and recommended sequencing:

- Regional capacity: us-west-2 has available GA100 capacity but constrained for immediate 2x burst across all AZs; eu-west-1 capacity will require a short provisioning lead (24–48h) for larger SKUs. See attached region map.
- Fallback tiers (recommended):
  1) us-west-2 primary (local pool)
  2) us-west-2 spare burst pool (same region, pre-warmed)
  3) eu-west-1 cold-fallback (cross-region, slightly higher latency)
  4) CloudOps partner pool (if both exhausted) — will incur cross-account routing overhead.
- SOW note: proposing a canary ramp schedule (5% / 25% / 60% over 48h) and a post-launch capacity review at Day+7. Draft SOW attached for review.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
